Closed at 25,466.19, up 400.31 points or 1.60% (Yahoo Finance), led by chip and AI stocks and erasing its post-election losses.
December crude settled near $86.41 a barrel, up $0.37 or 0.43% (Yahoo Finance), after trading near $87 in the afternoon (TheStreet).

themes.title: AI and chip stocks rebound
themes.summary: Tech carried the market after two days of losses; 18 of the S&P 500's top 20 performers in late morning were tech names (TheStreet), and SanDisk, Dell and Arm each closed up more than 11% (24/7 Wall St.).

themes.title: CoreWeave surges on results
themes.summary: CoreWeave closed up about 24% at $60.51 (24/7 Wall St.) after third-quarter revenue rose 168% to $3.7 billion and it raised its full-year outlook, though it still posted a $709 million net loss (TheStreet).

themes.title: Nvidia snaps a two-day slide
themes.summary: Nvidia rose about 3% to $173.73 but remains down roughly 12% to 14% in November (Yahoo Finance); Baird downgraded it to Neutral and its board is investigating reports involving CEO Jensen Huang (TheStreet).

themes.title: Fed hike still expected in December
themes.summary: After Tuesday's hotter-than-expected October CPI, traders see a December rate hike as nearly fully priced in, with about an 11% chance of a half-point move (TheStreet); the bond market was closed for Veterans Day.

themes.title: Oil edges up on Iran tensions
themes.summary: Crude posted a small gain as Iran's stance on the Strait of Hormuz kept supply concerns in focus (24/7 Wall St.); WTI remains well below the $100-plus levels seen before the midterm elections (TheStreet).

sectors.name: Technology
sectors.note: The top sector, up about 3.0% in the morning (24/7 Wall St.), led by semiconductors, storage and AI cloud names; Coherent and Monolithic Power gained more than 13% midday (TheStreet).

sectors.name: Energy / Industrials
sectors.note: Energy rose about 1.6% and industrials about 0.8% in the morning (24/7 Wall St.), with Bloom Energy closing up 12.5%.

sectors.name: Health Care / Consumer Staples / Consumer Discretionary
sectors.note: The laggards, down about 0.7%, 0.5% and 0.4% respectively in the morning (24/7 Wall St.); Lululemon, Clorox, Brown-Forman and Airbnb were among notable decliners (TheStreet).

sectors.name: Small Caps
sectors.note: The Russell 2000 opened down 0.68% (TheStreet) but finished up 0.79% at 2,848.04 (24/7 Wall St.).

watch_list.topic: Thursday: bond market reopens and earnings
watch_list.why: Treasury trading resumes after Veterans Day and the CPI-driven jump in yields; Nebius reports before the bell (Yahoo Finance) and Cisco reports this week (KuCoin).
